newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bills weaken at close, bond market deathly quiet.
newsitem.headline: NZ bills weaken at close, bond market deathly quiet.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (JUN) 92.25 (PREV 92.25) 90-DAYS 7.62 (PREV 7.60)
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.50 PCT (PREV 7.50) US 5-YR 6.63 (PREV 6.58)
* NZ bank bills weaken in afternoon despite NZD strength
* Bond market dead, trades two point range
* All eyes on FOMC meeting.
New Zealand bank bills were sold at Monday's close despite the currency retaining the strength that had encouraged morning buyers.
Dealers said weakness may indicate market scepticism about the Reserve Bank's inflation forecasts.
The bond market had one of the quietest days of the year, trading withing a two point range.
Dealers don't expect activity in the market to pick up until after Tuesday's FOMC meeting, and any decision on a U.S. rate hike is unlikely to emerge until Wednesday local time.
They said that with a cricket international in Wellington on Thursday and the short Easter week, activity could be limited to a 10 minute burst on Wednesday when the Fed announces its decision.
"Until that happens we aren't going to see any enthusiasm for our market," said one Wellington bond dealer.
The June bill futures closed at 92.25, against their morning high of 92.30. Volume was 1,255.
One bill dealer said there was an absence of bids and the tone was heavy.
"The market is a bit sceptical of whether the Reserve Bank can maintain its inflation forecasts," she said.
She said that according to the RB's inflation forecast assumptions, with the TWI at 68.3, bank bills should be nearer 7.30 percent than their current 7.6 percent.

"Why aren't they rallying? The market needs some inflation-friendly data to reassure us that the way we are going is up and even with the current government in power that the Reserve Bank can maintain its inflation track," she said.
